Preface: what this document is 
Hypergendered Logic (HGL) is the name given here to an invented formal field for reasoning about a 
recursively and hyperordinally defined fictional biology of Female, Male, Unfemale, Unmale, 
Suprafemale/Supramale, Hyperfemale/Hypermale, Ultrafemale/Ultramale, Apexfemale/Apexmale, further 
minor hypercategories, and the major-stage ladders of Archwomanhood and Archmanhood. The purpose of 
this document is not merely to list definitions. Its purpose is to make the underlying logic inspectable: to show 
where negation is located, which transformations are ordinary classical logic, which transformations are 
special HGL operations, which claims are strict deductions, which are logical inferences, which are causal 
deductions, which are causal inferences, and which phenotype examples are illustrative rather than forced. 
This is a fictional formal system, not a medical theory of real human sex development. In HGL, XX and XY 
are treated as formal chromosome-condition predicates because that is how the system has been defined. 
Real biological sex development is more complex than a two-predicate model. Accordingly, every biological 
example in this treatise is either (a) internal to the fictional HGL system, or (b) explicitly marked as an 
illustrative hypothetical phenotype rather than a real-world biological claim. 
Strengthened PA-Irreducibility + IH-Inheritance + PH-Phenotype + FD/UD Unflaw-Flaw + Significant-Quality 
+ Transcardinal-Quality + Limit-State Closure + SIH Superinheritance + Hyperdimensional Coordinate + 
Biological Metaexpression/Modal + Hypercategorical/Hyperordinal Revision. This edition retains the 
corrected PA-only SF1/SM1 base states and limit-complete SF/SM recursion, then adds an axis-typed 
Superinheritance operator SIH, strict category-lift transitions, recursively increasing Hyperfemale/Hypermale 
dimensional strata, subsequent Ultra and Apex dimensional families, and a full coordinate-vector 
Archaddress. 
AUTHORITATIVE PRECEDENCE — 17 AUGUST 2026: Part XLV and Appendices BO-BW are 
authoritative over every earlier boundary-identity statement, named-category map, active-axis 
existence statement, coordinate-successor rule, dimensional-limit rule, limit machine specification, 
quality-at-limit statement, proof catalogue, worked example, or compiler rule that conflicts with the 
Axis-Complete / Bounded-Superinheritance revision. Part XLIV remains authoritative for the 
six-role Supra LSCC Profile-Exclusion closure and the three-role Ultra/Apex UD strengthening. 
Part XLIII remains authoritative for the eight-conjunct SF2/SM2, six-conjunct ordinary Supra 
successor, and five-conjunct Hyper dimensional-lift recurrence. Current category order is Supra -> 
Hyper -> Ultra -> Apex. All category boundaries are strict constructions, never endpoint identities.

223. Canonical correction: phenotype versus meta-phenotype 
Phenotype, in the ordinary HGL sense, means a physically apparent or physically instantiated biological 
characteristic/configuration. It can be macroscopic or microscopic, local or systemic, temporary or persistent. 
Archwomanhood phenotype and Archmanhood phenotype are higher-order uses of the word phenotype. 
They are meta-phenotypes: stage-specific global rules and constraints over physical phenotype expression. 
To prevent type confusion, this treatise writes them as Γ^F_n and Γ^M_n. 
Γ^F_n := the global Stage-n Archwomanhood meta-phenotype function. 
Γ^M_n := the global Stage-n Archmanhood meta-phenotype function. 
P := an actual physically expressed phenotype state. 
The difference is the same kind of difference that exists between a parameter and a hyperparameter. P 
contains the biological outputs. Γ configures the rules that determine which outputs are available, required, 
excluded, or transformed. 
224. Why the hyperparameter analogy is structurally accurate 
Suppose a phenotype-generating system has ordinary biological variables θ: hormone concentrations,

274. Why this is stronger than a “whole-body trait” theory 
If an Archwomanhood phenotype were merely a whole-body trait, the theory would have to explain how one 
trait could literally be identical in skin, bone, liver, brain, blood, and reproductive anatomy. The 
meta-phenotype interpretation avoids that category error. What is global is the rule-regime, not the local trait 
identity. 
It is therefore more powerful to say that Stage 20 globally changes the laws of biological phenotype 
expressibility than to say that Stage 20 paints the same special trait onto every tissue. 
275. Why this makes modal logic an extension rather than an analogy 
Modal logic is not being added merely because words such as “possible” and “necessary” sound useful. Γ 
literally defines a space of admissible realizations. Quantifying over that space is modal semantics. 
necessity = truth in all Γ-valid phenotype realizations. 
possibility = truth in at least one Γ-valid phenotype realization. 
impossibility = truth in none of the Γ-valid phenotype realizations. 
The modal extension is therefore a direct formalization of Biological Metaexpressability. 
276. Developmental modality generated around PA 
A parallel but distinct modal layer can be used to reason about realizations of a PA developmental mode. Let 
D_φ be the set of developmental realizations compatible with the irreducible PA source φ. 
□^D_φ q := q holds in every admissible developmental realization of PA(φ). 
◇^D_φ q := q holds in at least one admissible developmental realization of PA(φ). 
These modal operators are not identical to PA itself. PA(φ) establishes the developmental causal mode due 
to φ. □^D_φ and ◇^D_φ quantify over how that mode may be realized.

Part XXXII — Macroscopic Anatomical and Outward Phenotypic 
Expression: authoritative modal correction 
This part is an authoritative refinement of the Biological Metaexpression and Modal Extension. It corrects any 
earlier wording that could be read as allowing a valid Archwomanhood or Archmanhood stage to be 
phenotypically global only in an internal, microscopic, latent, or purely counterfactual sense. The corrected 
canon is stronger: the Archstage meta-phenotype Γ is global because it governs phenotype expression 
throughout the body, and its domain explicitly includes gross anatomy and outward appearance. Therefore 
every valid Archfemale and Archmale stage has at least some stage-governed macroscopic anatomical 
expression and at least some outwardly apparent expression, even though many additional stage properties 
can remain microscopic, physiological, latent, internal, temporal, or counterfactual. 
AUTHORITATIVE CORRECTION​
Meta-level does not mean invisible. Global rule-governance does not mean merely internal 
rule-governance. Breasts, gross reproductive anatomy, external genital anatomy, body contour, 
facial and skeletal morphology, skin, hair, and other visually or gross-anatomically apparent 
physical characteristics are phenotypes and therefore fall inside the domain governed by Γ 
whenever they are biologically relevant to the subject. The exact form of those phenotypes 
remains underdetermined unless a specific phenotype law is supplied. 
233. Phenotype includes macroscopic anatomy and outward appearance 
In HGL, phenotype is not restricted to microscopic tissue states. A phenotype is a physically instantiated or 
physically apparent biological characteristic/configuration. Gross anatomical structures are phenotypes. 
Outwardly visible body characteristics are phenotypes. Internal macroscopic anatomy is also phenotype 
even when it is not externally visible. Thus the phenotype domain must be divided by scale and visibility 
rather than by a false internal-versus-phenotypic opposition. 
Macroscopic anatomical phenotype: gross structure that can be described at organ, regional, or whole-body 
scale. 
Outwardly apparent phenotype: physically observable external morphology or appearance. 
Internal macroscopic phenotype: gross anatomy that is physically real at macroscopic scale but not 
necessarily externally visible. 
Microscopic phenotype: tissue, cellular, microanatomical, or other small-scale physically instantiated 
characteristics. 
Physiological phenotype: physically instantiated functional characteristics, which may have visible, 
measurable, internal, or systemic consequences. 
Examples such as breast anatomy and gross reproductive anatomy demonstrate why a phenotype theory 
that focuses only on microscopic or hidden consequences is incomplete. A breast is a macroscopic 
anatomical phenotype. Vaginal anatomy is a macroscopic anatomical phenotype even though most of it is 
internal. External genital anatomy is both macroscopic and externally apparent. Body proportions, facial 
morphology, skin appearance, skeletal contours, hair distribution, and other outward physical characteristics 
are also phenotype domains. The male side is exactly parallel for male-typed gross anatomy and outward 
morphology. 
234. The domain-completeness rule for Γ 
The stage meta-phenotype Γ is a global biological metaexpression function. Globality now has an explicitly 
domain-complete interpretation: Γ governs the rules and constraints under which physical phenotypes may, 
must, cannot, and conditionally can express across every biologically relevant phenotype domain. This 
includes—not merely permits as an optional afterthought—macroscopic anatomy and outward appearance.

domain, including microscopic, physiological, internal-macroscopic, gross-anatomical, and

anatomical rule follows from stage order.

anatomy.

Macro/outward manifestation != every trait is visible. 
Meta-phenotype != hidden phenotype. 
Global rule-governance != uniform local morphology. 
Macroscopic != outward; internal gross anatomy is still macroscopic phenotype. 
Outwardly apparent != stage-diagnostic. 
Visible change != stage change. 
Stage change != necessarily large visible change. 
Higher order != monotone increase in any ordinary anatomical measurement. 
Same visible phenotype != same Γ. 
Different Γ != necessarily disjoint visible phenotype sets. 
PH-profile possession != Γ metaexpression. 
Γ metaexpression != PA developmental causation. 
263. Compact authoritative statement 
Every Archwomanhood and Archmanhood stage is a global biological metaexpression regime, not 
merely a hidden or microscopic state. The regime governs the rules and constraints of how 
female-typed or male-typed physical phenotypes can, must, cannot, and conditionally can express 
throughout the body. Because gross anatomy and outward appearance are phenotype domains, 
every valid Archstage necessarily has at least some stage-governed macroscopic anatomical and 
outwardly apparent realization. This requirement does not make every stage trait visible, does not 
make every stage visually unique, and does not make higher stage a scalar exaggeration. A static 
stage can continue producing changing visible womanhood/manhood outputs as ordinary 
development changes the parameters passed through the unchanged Γ.

Every scenario is fictional and is labeled by what it illustrates rather than asserted as canon. 
E.1 Joint-cause tissue 
An SF1 tissue appears only when the joint condition x∧¬y is the designated PA basis. Removing either 
constituent destroys that joint-cause attribution even if some similar tissue can arise another way. Lesson: 
PA irreducibility. 
E.2 Stage-2 route separation 
At SF2, three tissues are visually similar, but one traces to inherited SF1, one to standalone PAx, and one to 
standalone PA¬y. Lesson: phenotype similarity does not prove causal identity. 
E.3 Inherited non-SM1 gate 
A Stage-2 regulatory gate is active only because IH¬SM1 is present. Lesson: inherited non-state can be 
causally productive without being a PA mode. 
E.4 Stage-3 source sensitivity 
A cell responds differently to IH¬SM2 than it did to inherited ¬SM1. Lesson: source index can matter. 
E.5 Boolean redundancy, causal novelty 
The bare statement ¬SM8 is already implied by a stronger lower exclusion, but a protein complex specifically 
recognizes a biological marker associated with the IH source ¬SM8. Lesson: projection redundancy need not 
be causal redundancy. 
E.6 Delayed maturation 
An SF7 structure is established at stage acquisition but reaches its adult form only after ordinary puberty 
progresses. Lesson: stage acquisition and maturation separate. 
E.7 Permanent stage ceiling 
An Archfemale never passes SF5, yet ages from childhood to adulthood and continues to mature. Lesson: 
permanent Archstage stagnation is not biological arrest. 
E.8 Same stage, different age 
Two SF8 subjects are ages 13 and 30. They share stage but not maturity. Lesson: stage does not determine 
age. 
E.9 Same maturity, different stage 
Two adult Archfemales are SF3 and SF20. Both are sexually mature. Lesson: maturity does not determine 
stage. 
E.10 Hidden microanatomy 
SF15 produces no obvious external difference but creates a stage-specific microvascular network. Lesson: 
visibility is not required.

E.11 Functional novelty without anatomy 
SF16 modifies homeostatic coordination without creating a new gross anatomical structure. Lesson: HGL 
includes physiology. 
E.12 Anatomical novelty without stereotypical amplification 
SF18 creates a novel internal interface between two tissues rather than exaggerating familiar sex-associated 
features. Lesson: hidden dimension is not stereotype scaling. 
E.13 Repair phenotype 
A high-stage inherited source improves repair of an existing tissue. Lesson: later stages can change 
reliability/maintenance rather than size. 
E.14 Timing phenotype 
The endpoint anatomy is unchanged, but the developmental timing of maturation differs. Lesson: phenotype 
can include temporal physiology. 
E.15 Suppressive interaction 
A new inherited non-SM source suppresses an optional earlier pathway. Lesson: productivity can work by 
structured exclusion. 
E.16 Enabling interaction 
The same kind of source enables an earlier latent pathway that could not activate at lower order. Lesson: 
high-order input can recontextualize old structure. 
E.17 Three-way synergy 
A trait appears only when inherited SF4, inherited non-SM6, and adult maturity coexist. Lesson: nonlinear 
causal map. 
E.18 Convergent phenotype 
SF8 and SF12 arrive at similar visible anatomy through different internal pathways. Lesson: phenotype does 
not uniquely reveal stage. 
E.19 Divergent phenotype 
Two SF12 subjects differ because of environmental history. Lesson: stage need not uniquely determine 
phenotype.

F.1 A five-minute lay explanation 
Female and Male are not treated as volume knobs. Suprafemale and Supramale are recursive biological 
states. A compound condition inside PA creates an irreducible developmental route. A higher stage then 
keeps the previous stage through IH and also inherits the logical non-state of the opposite-side previous 
stage. That inheritance history can keep getting deeper forever in the finite sequence. The body can still 
mature normally while staying at one stage. 
F.2 A five-minute logician explanation 
HGL is a typed, non-homomorphic causal modal-like system with PA, IH, PH, UD/FD, SIH, LSCC, and 
Gamma as distinct operator families. PA accepts inner condition formulas but does not preserve 
conjunction/disjunction structure and is not generally monotone. IH accepts typed inheritable sources, 
projects to its operand, does not admit converse projection, and preserves source/depth as intensional 
identity. PH positively asserts complete whole-profile possession; NOT PH explicitly denies that possession 
and is not PH(NOT source). Current SF/SM recursion combines same-side IH, opposite structured-nonstate 
IH, same-side PH, opposite NOT-PH, same-side UD, and same-side NOT-FD. Female/Male category typing 
remains distinct from every one of these operators. 
F.3 A five-minute scientist explanation 
PA represents causal attribution of necessarily developable anatomy/physiology. IH represents retained 
developmental provenance. PH represents irreducible possession of a whole HGL phenotype-profile. Stage 
is therefore a structured causal/phenotypic history, not merely a label. To predict concrete phenotype, identify 
the stage’s PH nodes and profile map, active PA modes, IH provenance, maturity, environment, and history. 
Deduce profile membership when specified; do not invent concrete anatomy merely from a stage number. 
F.4 A five-minute AI explanation 
Use a typed AST. Keep PA, IH, PH, UD, and FD as distinct node types. Do not move NOT through PA, IH, 
PH, UD, or FD without an explicit rule. Do not distribute PA/IH/PH/UD/FD. Preserve IH provenance and PA 
irreducibility. Canonicalize SF1/SM1 as PA-only bases, SF2/SM2 as eight-conjunct bases, and Stage 3+ as 
six-conjunct successors. Track whole-form quality Q and magnitude K separately from category membership 
and from local phenotype measurements. Proof-trace every D/HI/CD/CI conclusion.

14. Canonical Supramale Stage 1 
The canonical first Supramale state is the exact PA-only mirror. 
SM1 = PA(NOT x AND y) 
In full condition labels: SM1 = PA(NOT XX AND XY). 
SM1 contains one constitutive developmental-causal mode, PA(NOT x AND y), with the compound source 
preserved irreducibly. 
Strict deduction from the definition: SM1 entails PA(NOT x AND y). No condition-source IH term, PH term, 
UD term, or FD term is constitutive of SM1. 
PA irreducibility blocks SM1 => PA(NOT x) and SM1 => PA(y) as general deductions. Those standalone 
routes first appear explicitly in SM2. 
MaleType(SM1) remains a separate category axiom, not a PA-distribution rule. 
PH(SM1) enters canonically at SM2 as positive same-side whole-profile possession. The opposite 
whole-profile is instead excluded by NOT PH(SF1). General-language PH(NOT SF1) remains syntactically 
legal but is not constitutive SM2 content. 
15. Stage-2 phenotype antithesis versus ordinary non-possession 
PH(NOT S) remains a legal positive phenotype-profile possession statement whose source is a logical 
non-state, and it is not equivalent to NOT PH(S). However, the current canonical SF/SM successor 
definitions deliberately use NOT PH(opposite), not PH(NOT opposite). The distinction is therefore both 
semantically and constitutively important. 
This distinction becomes constitutively decisive at Stage 2: SF2 contains NOT PH(SM1), while SM2 contains 
NOT PH(SF1). These are negative whole-profile-possession claims. They do not assert possession of the 
phenotype-profile of the structured non-state. 
Thus the phenotype counterpart of the PA/IH scope lesson remains canonical, but it is no longer incorrectly 
attributed to constitutive Stage-1 PH terms.

current Stage-3+ successor formula produces approximately six predecessor-subtree copies: four own-side

opposite) and NOT PH(opposite). Thus T(n+1)=6T(n)+O(1) and naive textual/tree size is Theta(6^n). This is

carries six typed recursive operator edges, but those edges target only two unique predecessor-state 
objects: the own-side predecessor and the opposite-side predecessor. Repeated references do not duplicate 
the referenced stage object. Provenance remains exact because edge labels preserve 
IH/PH/NOT-PH/UD/NOT-FD role and source identity.

represented intensionally by an ordinal bound, not extensionally by an impossible-to-enumerate list when the

Appendix T — Formal stage-relative modal semantics 
T.1 Model structure 
A metaexpressive HGL model can be represented as M = <B,H,E,W,Γ,V>, with separate female-side and 
male-side stage-indexed Γ functions. B is biological state, H is developmental history, E is 
environment/context, W is a family of admissible phenotype realization sets, and V evaluates phenotype 
propositions. 
T.2 Female accessibility relation 
w R^F_n v := v is a Γ^F_n-valid phenotype realization accessible from biological/context state w. 
w |= □^F_n φ iff for every v, w R^F_n v implies v |= φ. 
w |= ◇^F_n φ iff for some v, w R^F_n v and v |= φ. 
T.3 Male accessibility relation 
w R^M_n v := v is a Γ^M_n-valid phenotype realization accessible from biological/context state w. 
The female and male accessibility relations are structurally symmetric unless a specific HGL law introduces 
an asymmetry. 
T.4 Why the actual realization is accessible 
For a correctly classified valid subject, the actual phenotype world is one of the phenotype realizations 
licensed by the current Γ. This gives the stage modality its T/factivity behavior. 
T.5 No automatic S4/S5 
The biological accessibility relation is not presumed transitive, symmetric, Euclidean, or reflexively 
introspective beyond the actual-validity condition. A body being able to reach phenotype v from phenotype w 
does not imply reverse reachability, and a phenotype possibility about another possibility is not automatically 
flattened. 
T.6 Modal equivalence versus phenotype equivalence 
Two subjects can share all currently observed phenotype propositions while differing in R_n and therefore 
differing in what they could express under counterfactual biological conditions. 
CurrentPhenotype(a)=CurrentPhenotype(b) does not imply R(a)=R(b). 
T.7 Fixed-address normality 
For each fixed valid Archaddress a, the adopted Kripke-style semantics is a normal address-relative 
modality. Therefore the K distribution law is valid: Box_a(phi -> psi) -> (Box_a(phi) -> Box_a(psi)). This is a 
logical property of the modality at one address, not a biological assertion that later stages preserve every 
possibility. 
T.8 Necessitation rule, narrowly typed 
If phi is a theorem valid in every world of the relevant model class, the normal modal rule permits inferring 
Box_a(phi). Necessitation does NOT license actual(phi) -> Box_a(phi), observed(phi) -> Box_a(phi), or 
possible(phi) -> Box_a(phi). A contingent biological truth does not become necessary merely because it 
actually occurs.

T.9 Stage-Modal Strengthening is not modal necessitation 
When a trait is possible at one Archaddress and necessary at another, call that a Stage-Modal Strengthening 
or address-relative modal-status change. Do not call it the rule of necessitation. This terminodistinction 
prevents proof-system necessitation from being confused with biological evolution of the accessible 
phenotype-space. 
T.10 No cross-address monotonicity axiom 
HGL does not adopt W_a subseteq W_b merely because b is a later address, nor the reverse inclusion. A 
later Gamma may open possibilities, close possibilities, make a possibility necessary, make a former 
necessity merely possible, or restructure trait compatibility. Rule-structural enrichment is therefore not 
identical to set-theoretic expansion of accessible phenotype worlds. 
Appendix U — Biological Metaexpressability proof catalogue 
U.1 Proof: global governance does not imply uniform output 
Let Γ act on two regions r1 and r2 with different biological inputs B1 and B2. Let the stage-valid outputs be 
P1=Γ(B1) and P2=Γ(B2), with P1≠P2. Γ is global because it governs both regions. Therefore global 
governance is consistent with nonuniform local phenotype. 
U.2 Proof: static Γ does not imply static phenotype 
Let Γ be constant and let θ1≠θ2. Choose a nonconstant phenotype-generation function F such that 
F(θ1;Γ)≠F(θ2;Γ). Then Γ constancy and phenotype change are jointly satisfiable. Therefore Γ(t1)=Γ(t2) does 
not logically entail P(t1)=P(t2). 
U.3 Proof: actual entails possible 
By validity, the actual phenotype realization belongs to W_n. If p is true at that actual realization, there exists 
at least one W_n realization satisfying p. Hence ◇_n p. 
U.4 Proof: necessity entails actuality 
If □_n p, p holds at every W_n realization. The actual valid realization is a member of W_n. Therefore p holds 
actually. 
U.5 Countermodel: possibility does not entail actuality 
Let W_n contain two realizations v1 and v2. Let p be true only at v2 while v1 is actual. Then ◇_n p is true 
but p is not actual. 
U.6 Countermodel: same stage does not imply same phenotype 
Let two subjects share Γ_n but have different maturity vectors θA and θB. If F is sensitive to maturity, their 
outputs differ while stage remains the same. 
U.7 Countermodel: same phenotype does not imply same stage 
Let Γ_3 and Γ_20 both permit current output p while differing on a counterfactual phenotype q. The two 
subjects can currently express p identically even though ◇_20 q and NOT ◇_3 q distinguish their stages.

Appendix W — Modal deduction/inference decision table in prose 
W.1 When to call something a deduction 
Call a modal phenotype statement a deduction only when it follows from the current Γ definition, the adopted 
modal semantics, an explicit PH profile membership, an IH projection, a PA rule, or an explicit causal bridge. 
Name the rule used. 
W.2 When to call something a logical inference 
Use HGL inference when the architecture strongly suggests richer possibility-space, greater context 
sensitivity, or deeper rule interactions at higher stages but no theorem forces the exact claim. 
W.3 When to call something a causal deduction 
Use causal deduction when an explicit rule maps a satisfied developmental/metaexpressive antecedent to a 
particular phenotype consequence. 
W.4 When to call something a causal inference 
Use causal inference when the model makes a generative relationship plausible—for example, changing 
puberty inputs under static Γ plausibly yielding new female phenotype—but no complete causal law uniquely 
determines the phenotype.

meta-phenotypic. It is the stage-level biological metaexpression function Γ through which actual physical 
phenotypes throughout the body are governed. Actual phenotypes themselves can remain local. PH remains

The revised Hypergendered Logic can be summarized as a theory of causally irreducible developmental 
modes embedded in a provenance-preserving inheritance ladder, explicit whole-source phenotype-profile 
possession, and global stage-specific biological metaexpression functions whose modal spaces govern 
actual phenotype expression. 
At low order, novelty can come from PA causal scope and irreducible PH profiles. At higher order, novelty 
comes from deeper IH/PH source structure and from Γ-level changes in the rules, constraints, dimensions, 
and counterfactual possibilities of phenotype expression. The female and male ladders recursively define 
one another’s next inherited non-opposite input while each current stage globally governs how its actual 
physical phenotypes may, must, or cannot express. 
The hierarchy’s strongest conceptual promise is therefore not “more female” or “more male” as a scalar. It is 
the systematic possibility of discovering deeper female-typed or male-typed biological metaexpression 
structures: new irreducible developmental bases, new inherited provenance, new PH whole-profiles, and 
new stage-relative possibilities, necessities, impossibilities, conditional relations, and latent phenotype 
dimensions. A stage can remain fixed while ordinary womanhood/manhood development continues because 
the fixed Γ continues governing changing biological parameters.

238. Flaw and Unflaw: exact canonical definitions 
Flaw: a physically instantiated feature whose presence decreases the quality of ANY extent of the physical 
structure or form. FD(a). 
Unflaw: a physically instantiated feature whose presence significantly increases the quality of the whole 
physical structure and form. UD(a). 
The capitalization of ANY is semantically important. FD is locally sensitive: if the presence of a produces a 
quality decrease in even one relevant physical extent, region, component, relation, or organized part, then a 
can satisfy FD(a), even if other parts improve. UD is globally demanding: the presence of a must significantly 
increase the quality of the physical structure/form considered as a whole. The predicates therefore test 
different scopes and are not logical negations of one another. 
NOT FD(a) does not entail UD(a) 
FD(a) does not entail NOT UD(a) 
UD(a) does not entail NOT FD(a), unless an additional incompatibility axiom is explicitly adopted 
A neutral feature supplies the simplest countermodel to NOT FD(a) -> UD(a): the feature lowers no local 
quality but also fails to produce a significant whole-form improvement. A mixed-effect feature supplies a 
countermodel to FD(a) -> NOT UD(a): it may worsen one local extent while producing an overwhelmingly 
larger, significant increase in whole-form quality. HGL therefore deliberately permits FD(a) AND UD(a) unless 
a future axiom forbids mixed effects. The current recursion goes further by explicitly requiring NOT FD of the 
own-side predecessor, thereby ruling out that mixed-effect possibility for that particular inherited predecessor 
role while independently asserting UD of it.

303. SIH — exact canonical definition 
SIH means Superinherits. Let Omega denote the typed HGL Hyperomega bound for the axis being

the terminal member.

Part XX — The entire revised theory in layman’s terms 
Imagine ordinary female or male biology as a large biological language. Archwomanhood and Archmanhood 
are not volume knobs that turn “female” or “male” above 100%. They are recursive ways of building 
increasingly deep grammatical history into that biology. 
PA answers: what developmental condition makes this anatomy/physiology necessarily developable? If two 
conditions are joined inside PA, the development can depend irreducibly on them together. That is why PA(A 
AND B) is not just PA(A) AND PA(B). 
IH answers a different question: what properties does this higher stage carry forward from an earlier state, 
and where did those properties come from? If a Stage-5 Archfemale inherits Stage 4, she does not merely 
happen to resemble Stage 4. Her Stage-5 state explicitly carries Stage-4 structure as inherited history. 
IH(NOT SM4) does not mean “she simply failed to inherit SM4.” It means her state inherits the structured 
condition of not being SM4. That is how the zig-zag becomes productive: the female ladder takes the logical 
non-state of the latest male ladder and makes it inherited material in the next female stage. The male ladder 
does the mirror image. 
The ladder therefore grows by two simultaneous actions: 
keep your own previous stage; inherit the non-state of the other side’s previous stage. 
Because every new stage wraps the old stage in another inheritance relation, the number of inheritance 
layers can grow without limit even though PA itself never nests. 
Finally, stage and maturity are different. If an Archfemale stays at Stage 6 for ten years, she can still continue 
puberty, sexual maturation, aging, and maturation of Stage-6 structures. She keeps developing as a woman 
even though she is not currently climbing higher as an Archwoman. The same applies to Archmales.

Part XXIV — Remaining open questions after the IH revision 
The following are genuine open variables. Earlier questions about the canonical whole-state antithesis 
operator, SF2 conflict, and Stage-1 female typing are closed by the present revision and are no longer open. 
75. Which logically equivalent source formulas count as the same IH source? 
The conservative assumption is that classically equivalent descriptions of one source state can be 
normalized without changing source identity, while derivational provenance is retained separately. A future 
intensional refinement could distinguish syntactic histories even when Boolean content is equivalent. 
76. Exactly which properties are “inheritable properties”? 
Core IH projection says all source-state content relevant to HGL is retained. A fuller theory could partition 
properties into constitutive, optional, transient, or noninheritable classes. Until then, IH(S) should be read 
as inheritance of the source state’s HGL-defining properties, not literally every accidental fact true of the 
individual who once occupied S. 
77. Can IH ever distribute under a special law? 
Core HGL says no automatic distribution. A future rule could state that particular outer conjunctions are 
componentwise inheritable, but such a rule must preserve PA irreducibility and source provenance. 
78. Can a stage be lost or regress? 
The present ladder defines upward construction and permits stagnation. Regression requires a separate 
temporal law. 
79. Can stages be skipped? 
Not specified. The canonical recursive definition gives an order, but a causal transition theory would need to 
say whether an individual must physically pass through every preceding stage.

180. Final statement of the revised insight 
Hypergendered Logic now has a clear answer to the question “what grows at higher order?” The answer is 
not PA nesting, not chromosome percentage, not repeated bare negation, and not arbitrary new labels. What 
grows is a source-preserving inheritance architecture whose own-side past and opposite-side logical 
non-state are recursively carried into each new stage. 
This produces a hierarchy that can be indefinitely deep in the finite sense while keeping the spoken biology 
coherent: 
An Archfemale at a higher stage inherits the complete developmental architecture of the prior 
Archwomanhood stage and inherits the structured non-state of the corresponding prior 
Archmanhood stage. An Archmale does the mirror image. The stage explicitly determines its PH 
phenotype-profiles, while the concrete contents/expression of those profiles and additional 
woman/man phenotypes depend on the fictional phenotype map, maturity, and causal realization; 
the female/male category direction remains fixed. 
Part XXIX — The PH Phenotype-Possession Revision: authoritative 
integration 
This part is the authoritative phenotype-layer expansion of HGL. It must be read together with the 
PA-Irreducibility and IH-Inheritance rules. Where an earlier phenotype discussion said merely that “stage 
logic does not determine phenotype,” the corrected statement is now more precise: 
A stage formula containing PH terms does determine that the corresponding irreducible HGL 
phenotype-profiles are possessed. What remains underdetermined until the profile map is 
supplied is the concrete anatomical/physiological content of those profiles and any additional 
non-stage phenotype produced by maturity, environment, history, or emergence. 
That distinction removes a false dilemma between “HGL says nothing about phenotype” and “HGL fixes 
every visible body trait.” The correct theory lies between them.
